previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission after allogeneic cord transplant, chronic kidney disease, and systolic heart failure, was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. He was diagnosed with adenovirus gastroenteritis, confirmed by positive stool and blood viral cultures, and treated with a single dose of cidofovir and IVIG, leading to viral clearance. His hospital course was complicated by a recurrent perirectal abscess requiring incision and drainage, multifocal pneumonia that progressed to acute respiratory failure necessitating 6 days of mechanical ventilation, and acute on chronic systolic heart failure with pulmonary edema managed with diuresis. He also developed acute tubular necrosis, likely secondary to cidofovir and volume fluctuations, with creatinine stabilizing by discharge. His macrocytic anemia worsened, with hemoglobin dropping to 7.2 g/dL, but he declined a bone marrow biopsy. HHV-6 levels peaked but resolved without treatment. He was discharged home with services on Lasix, fluconazole, adjusted Bactrim prophylaxis, and a nebulizer, with follow-up planned for lab monitoring and iron chelation evaluation.
problems: Abscess of anal and rectal regions
Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Acute kidney failure with lesion of tubular necrosis

Brief Hospital Course:
___ M with PMH AML s/p BMT in ___ complicated by GVHD (cellcept 
recently discontinued), CKD III, HTN, GERD, with recent 
admission for diarrhea and N/V found to be adenovirus positive, 
again admitted for diarrhea and nausea/vomiting. 

# Likely acute GI infection: 
GVHD less likely given improvement in symptoms without high dose 
steroids. Had recent admission for similar symptoms and was 
found to have adenovirus, was treated with IVIG and cidofivir 
during that prior admission. Reports family members at home have 
had abdominal symptoms. C diff, stool studies, and stool 
norovirus negative. Adenovirus PCR sent and pending as of 
discharge. Pt was given IV fluids. Was initially npo but 
tolerated regular low residue lactose free diet prior to 
discharge. Diarrhea resolved, and pt felt well prior to 
discharge, without abdominal pain or nausea.

# Acute on chronic renal failure: 
Baseline creatinine ~2.0-2.5. Likely prerenal in setting of poor 
po and GI losses. Improved with IV fluids, from 4.0 on admission 
to 2.7 at discharge.

# Non-gap metabolic acidosis: 
Likely due to GI losses from diarrhea in the setting of renal 
impairment.

# Chemotherapy induced systolic heart failure: 
Last echo (___) shows LVEF ___. Pt was initially given 
IV fluids. Home lasix (60mg po daily) was held during admission. 
Continued on home metoprolol and aspirin. Discharge weight: 
214.9 lbs. Pt will be discharged on lasix 40mg po daily.

# AML s/p BMT in ___, Chronic GVHD: 
Was on cellcept previously, had been discontinued prior to 
admission. Continued on prednisone 3mg daily, Bactrim SS daily, 
and valacyclovir. HHV-6 sent and pending as of discharge.

# Hyperkalemia: 
K was 5.4 in ED, likely due to renal failure in setting of 
infection. Resolved with IV fluids.

# Depression:
Continued on escitalopram.

# GERD:
Continued on pantoprazole.

# Allergic rhinitis:
Continued on loratidine.
